scope.frame: the weave of 2g records on a genus-g surface with one boundary (the mapping classes acting on F_2g)
scope.object: the characters fixed by every move: SL(2, C), the Heisenberg groups H(p), the extraspecial 2-groups
scope.hypotheses: W109 (ii) for the handle step (verified in B1679); the numerical search for (a) is evidence, the proof the claim

claim_one_line: W111 ON MAIN (P-211; Review 67's R67-6; the proof read step by step, the transvection lemma re-derived by hand, the checks recomputed by main's own code): on a genus-g surface with one boundary the only SL(2, C) character fixed by the mapping classes is the trivial one from g = 2 on (at g = 1 also the quaternion point), the odd-p Heisenberg character is fixed at every genus, and an extraspecial 2-group character is fixed only at g = 1, where it is Q8; main's checks: every move keeps the boundary class (g = 1-3), the g = 2 search finds only the trivial character (21 of 40 starts converge, all trivial; the g = 1 control finds trivial and quaternion), H(3) and H(5) fixed at g = 1, 2, and of the Pauli representations only g = 1 with all squares -I is fixed, the all-minus g = 2 case broken by mu' alone. So on the surface route two records come from the prime 2 that the rank-two target forces, not from extending the moves. 0 of 19.
weave_or_thread: weave (every move of the surface route, every character of the stated kind)
